title: Minimal probe-limit holographic superconductor
summary: A linear-onset and nonlinear-boundary-value reproduction of the dimension-two condensate in the minimal probe-limit AdS4 holographic-superconductor model.

conventions.name: background and coordinate
conventions.value: Planar AdS4-Schwarzschild probe limit; u = r_h/r in [0,1], f(u) = 1-u^3, L = r_h = 1 during the solve
conventions.rationale: Makes the horizon and UV boundary finite endpoints and isolates scale-invariant observables.

conventions.name: matter sector
conventions.value: Real charged scalar psi(u), electric potential A_t = phi(u), m^2 L^2 = -2, q = 1
conventions.rationale: Conventions of the source model after fixing the charge unit.

conventions.name: UV gauge source
conventions.value: phi = mu - rho u + ... with nonzero chemical potential mu
conventions.rationale: The chemical potential is the boundary gauge-field source and is not set to zero.

conventions.name: UV scalar quantization
conventions.value: psi = psi_- u + psi_+ u^2 + ...; Delta = 2 quantization with psi_- = 0
conventions.rationale: The scalar source vanishes while psi_+ gives spontaneous condensation.

conventions.name: ensembles and plotted ratios
conventions.value: Grand-canonical onset reported through T_c/mu; condensate curve presented at fixed rho through T/T_c and sqrt(<O_2>)/T_c
conventions.rationale: Separates the nonzero gauge source from the fixed-density presentation used by Figure 1.

parameters.name: scalar mass squared
parameters.description: Mass used for both normalizable AdS4 scalar falloffs.

parameters.name: scalar charge
parameters.description: Set by the source's field-rescaling convention.

parameters.name: radial cutoff
parameters.description: Regulates both singular coordinate endpoints; its effect is checked numerically.

equations.description: Charged scalar equation in the fixed planar black-brane background.
equations.source_ref: Source Eq. (6), transformed from r to u = r_h/r.

equations.description: Maxwell equation coupled to the scalar condensate.
equations.source_ref: Source Eq. (7), transformed from r to u = r_h/r.

observables.name: critical temperature
observables.extraction: Linear vanishing-scalar-source eigenvalue in the normal gauge background, followed by the black-brane scaling relation.

observables.name: dimension-two condensate curve
observables.extraction: UV response coefficient psi_+ along nonlinear vanishing-scalar-source solutions, rescaled to the fixed-density Figure 1 presentation.

acceptance_criteria: The scalar-source residual is below 1e-8 at onset and along the nonlinear branch.
The nonlinear boundary-value collocation residual satisfies the configured numerical tolerance.
The critical value T_c/sqrt(rho) agrees with the source's rounded 0.118 within an absolute tolerance of 0.001.
The near-critical coefficient agrees within 5 percent with source Eq. (12).
The regenerated dimension-two curve is monotonic and reaches the Figure 1 low-temperature plateau between 8.2 and 8.7.

tests.expected: mu_c/r_h and T_c/sqrt(rho) reproduce the documented vanishing-scalar-source instability.
The dimension-two branch reproduces the near-critical coefficient and low-temperature plateau.
Representative onset and nonlinear observables remain stable when the cutoff is reduced.

claims.statement: For the Delta = 2 boundary condition, the source reports T_c approximately 0.118 sqrt(rho) and a condensate curve shown in Figure 1's right panel.
claims.evidence: Hartnoll, Herzog, and Horowitz, arXiv:0803.3295v1, Eqs. (10)-(12) and Figure 1.

claims.statement: The HoloForge implementation numerically reproduces the linear critical point and the dimension-two nonlinear condensate curve within its declared acceptance gates.
claims.evidence: Automated onset, continuation, cutoff-refinement, and curve tests in tests/test_holographic_superconductor.py.

limitations: The calculation neglects backreaction of the matter fields on the metric and is not a controlled zero-temperature solution.
The benchmark does not compute optical conductivity, free energy, or quasinormal modes.
The minimal boundary U(1) is global unless an additional weak gauging prescription is supplied; charged superfluid is then the more precise term.
The numerical endpoints use finite radial cutoffs and the plotted low-temperature plateau remains within the probe approximation of the source.
No fit to a real superconducting material is attempted.
